body.text: The country is split 52–48 on the AR-15 case — inside the margin of error, which makes it a tie.

Marquette Law School's new Supreme Court poll is the first citable public-opinion measurement on the December cases: 52% want the Court to find no right to own an AR-15, 48% the opposite, on a 3.3-point margin of error. It tightens to 50–49 among likely voters. Report it as a tie — never as majority support for either side, and never as a prediction of the ruling.

facts.title: 3. AR-15 cases — up on the poll, not the docket

body.text:
• DOJ's Minnesota deadline passed today with no filing, no docket entry, no announcement — expected, and not a result.
• This is NOT the AP-NORC poll (held unverified, run 7). Marquette's numbers are citable; AP-NORC's are not.
• Third consecutive run in which the OLC and ATF standing checks could not be executed. Decay, not doubt.
• Peer watch day 23: no structural move, and no peer has written on the poll, the OLC opinion or the NFA non-appeal.

This edition was produced by a manual run. No brief has reached Teams since 09/21 — the generation task was fine, but the Windows push task has not run, so 09/22 is staged and unpublished. Both editions publish on the next push; 09/22 will be in the archive but will not post its own card.
